components.note: 告 (gào) — loose hint — 靠 is kào; 告 also sounds out 造 zào and 酷 kù.
非 (not) — two wings pointing away from each other, so back to back; as a memory aid, 靠 is leaning your back on something.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.hanzi: 别靠近那条狗,它可能会咬人。
example.pinyin: Bié kàojìn nà tiáo gǒu, tā kěnéng huì yǎo rén.
example.english: Don't get close to that dog, it might bite.
example.fact: 靠 alone means "to lean against, to rely on" (as in 靠墙, "leaning against the wall") — combined with 近 ("near"), 靠近 literally means "to lean in near," a physical sense of approaching that also underlies the more abstract 靠得住 ("reliable," literally "able to be leaned on").

examples.hanzi: 请不要靠近那个危险的地方。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bú yào kàojìn nà ge wēixiǎn de dìfang.
examples.english: Please don't go near that dangerous place.

examples.hanzi: 夏天快要靠近了,天气越来越热。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān kuài yào kàojìn le, tiānqì yuè lái yuè rè.
examples.english: Summer is drawing near and the weather is getting hotter.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharpness: 利, 别, 到; 刻 is to carve, and the carved marks on a clock became quarter hours.
亥 (hài) is only a loose sound hint; same part in 孩 hái and 核 hé.

example.hanzi: 现在是三点一刻。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn yí kè.
example.english: It's a quarter past three now.
example.fact: 刻 as a unit of time literally means "to carve, to engrave" — a name traditionally traced back to the graduated marks carved onto ancient water clocks (刻漏) used to track the passing of quarter-hours, the same character root behind 时刻 ("moment") and 深刻 ("profound," literally "deeply carved").

examples.hanzi: 我们八点一刻在门口见面。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bā diǎn yí kè zài ménkǒu jiànmiàn.
examples.english: We'll meet at the entrance at a quarter past eight.

examples.hanzi: 就在那一刻,她明白了他的意思。
examples.pinyin: Jiù zài nà yí kè, tā míngbai le tā de yìsi.
examples.english: At that very moment, she understood what he meant.

components.note: 广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 你应该早点休息。
example.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi zǎodiǎn xiūxi.
example.english: You should rest earlier.
example.fact: 应 is read yīng in 应该 and 应当 (should), but yìng for "to respond" in 回应 and 应用 (to apply). 答应 (dāying, to promise) has a neutral second syllable.

examples.hanzi: 你应该多喝水。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ.
examples.english: You should drink more water.

examples.hanzi: 朋友有困难，我们应当帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou yǒu kùnnan, wǒmen yīngdāng bāngmáng.
examples.english: When a friend is in trouble, we ought to help.

components.note: 饣 (food) — 饣 is the simplified 食 (food), as in 饭, 饺, 饿; 饼 is a flat baked cake.
并 (bìng) — near sound — 饼 is bǐng; 并 also sounds out 拼 pīn.

example.hanzi: 中秋节我们吃月饼。
example.pinyin: Zhōngqiūjié wǒmen chī yuèbǐng.
example.english: We eat mooncakes at the Mid-Autumn Festival.
example.fact: 饼 covers any flat round food, not just sweet ones: 月饼 (mooncake), 煎饼 (thin savoury pancake), 烧饼 (sesame flatbread). 饼干 is a biscuit or cracker.

examples.hanzi: 这个饼又香又脆。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bǐng yòu xiāng yòu cuì.
examples.english: This pancake is fragrant and crispy.

examples.hanzi: 我早上常吃一个饼和一杯豆浆。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang cháng chī yí gè bǐng hé yì bēi dòujiāng.
examples.english: In the morning I often have a pancake and a cup of soy milk.

components.note: 见 (see) — 见 as in 现, 观, 觉; 规 first meant a compass, the drawing tool that sets the standard — hence rules, as in 规矩 compass and square.
夫 (fū) — loose sound hint — 规 is guī.
刂 (knife) — cutting and sharp edges: 利 sharp, 刻 carve, 别 divide; 则 meant rules engraved to last. 贝 here is simplified from old 鼎.

example.hanzi: 请大家遵守比赛规则。
example.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā zūnshǒu bǐsài guīzé.
example.english: Everyone please follow the rules of the competition.
example.fact: 规 originally named a craftsman's compass — a tool for drawing perfect circles — while 则 (built from 贝, a shell once used as currency, plus a knife 刂ancient laws being inscribed) named an inscribed standard; 规则 pairs "measuring tool" with "inscribed standard" into today's word for "rule."

examples.hanzi: 这个游戏的规则很简单。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì de guīzé hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: The rules of this game are very simple.

examples.hanzi: 他每天的生活都很有规则。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān de shēnghuó dōu hěn yǒu guīzé.
examples.english: His daily life is very regular.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我昨天接到了一个奇怪的电话。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān jiēdào le yí gè qíguài de diànhuà.
example.english: I received a strange phone call yesterday.
example.fact: 接到 pairs the verb 接 ("to receive, to catch") with the result complement 到 ("to arrive, to reach") — a common Mandarin pattern where a directional or result verb tacked onto a main verb confirms the action actually succeeded, the same construction behind 看到 ("to catch sight of") and 听到 ("to hear").

examples.hanzi: 我刚才接到了妈妈的电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāngcái jiēdào le māma de diànhuà.
examples.english: I just received a call from my mom.

examples.hanzi: 她接到通知,明天要去开会。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiēdào tōngzhī, míngtiān yào qù kāihuì.
examples.english: She got notified that she has to go to a meeting tomorrow.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 为了通过考试,他付出了很多努力。
example.pinyin: Wèile tōngguò kǎoshì, tā fùchū le hěn duō nǔlì.
example.english: To pass the exam, he put in a lot of effort.
example.fact: Unlike plain 付 or 花钱 ("to spend money"), 付出 is reserved for paying out something abstract — effort, time, a price, a sacrifice — almost never actual cash; for handing over money in a transaction, Chinese instead uses 付 or 支付.

examples.hanzi: 成功需要时间,也需要付出。
examples.pinyin: Chénggōng xūyào shíjiān, yě xūyào fùchū.
examples.english: Success takes time, and it also takes effort.

examples.hanzi: 你要为自己的选择付出代价。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào wèi zìjǐ de xuǎnzé fùchū dàijià.
examples.english: You have to pay a price for your choices.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 每个队员都要参加训练。
example.pinyin: Měi gè duìyuán dōu yào cānjiā xùnliàn.
example.english: Every team member has to attend training.
example.fact: 员 is one of Mandarin's most productive occupational suffixes — attach it to almost any group or role and it names a member of it (队员 "team member", 学员 "trainee", 演员 "actor", 售货员 "salesperson") — a pattern that traces back to 员's old sense of a counted, registered official.

examples.hanzi: 这位队员踢进了一个漂亮的球。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi duìyuán tījìn le yí ge piàoliang de qiú.
examples.english: This team member scored a beautiful goal.

examples.hanzi: 新队员今天第一次来训练。
examples.pinyin: Xīn duìyuán jīntiān dì yī cì lái xùnliàn.
examples.english: The new team member came to training for the first time today.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 for cloth and wearables, as in 布, 帐, 带; 帽 is a cloth head covering.
冒 (mào) — same sound — 帽 is mào, matching 冒.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 外面很冷,记得戴帽子。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, jìde dài màozi.
example.english: It's cold outside, remember to wear a hat.
example.fact: Beyond the literal hat, 帽子 shows up figuratively as an unwanted label pinned on someone — 扣帽子 ("to slap a hat on someone") describes unfairly branding a person with a damning accusation, an idiom especially associated with the political campaigns of Cultural-Revolution-era China.

examples.hanzi: 这顶帽子是我妈妈送给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dǐng màozi shì wǒ māma sòng gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This hat was a gift from my mom.

examples.hanzi: 他一进门就摘下了帽子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí jìn mén jiù zhāi xià le màozi.
examples.english: He took off his hat as soon as he came in.

components.note: 十 (ten, many) — traditional 協 pairs 十 with three 力 (strength) side by side: many forces joined in effort, so cooperation.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 两家公司签了一份协议。
example.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī qiān le yí fèn xiéyì.
example.english: The two companies signed an agreement.
example.fact: 协议 also does technical duty in computing as "protocol" (网络协议, "network protocol") — the same word covers a diplomatic pact and a data-transfer standard, since both describe two parties agreeing in advance on a shared set of rules.

examples.hanzi: 双方终于达成了协议。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng zhōngyú dáchéng le xiéyì.
examples.english: The two sides finally reached an agreement.

examples.hanzi: 你同意这份协议吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tóngyì zhè fèn xiéyì ma?
examples.english: Do you agree to this contract?

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 我花了很长时间才说服他改变主意。
example.pinyin: Wǒ huā le hěn cháng shíjiān cái shuōfú tā gǎibiàn zhǔyi.
example.english: It took me a long time to persuade him to change his mind.
example.fact: 服 by itself already means "to submit, to yield" (as in 服从, "to obey"), so 说服 is literally "to talk someone into submission" — fitting for a character whose own picture shows a hand fitting a garment onto a person, an image of being outfitted into compliance.

examples.hanzi: 我想说服妈妈让我养一只小狗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shuōfú māma ràng wǒ yǎng yì zhī xiǎo gǒu.
examples.english: I want to persuade Mom to let me have a puppy.

examples.hanzi: 他的话很有说服力。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà hěn yǒu shuōfú lì.
examples.english: His words are very convincing.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.

example.hanzi: 上周我们去爬山了。
example.pinyin: Shàngzhōu wǒmen qù páshān le.
example.english: Last week we went hiking.
example.fact: 上 here isn't "above" but "previous" in a time sequence — the same 上 shows up in 上个月 ("last month") and 上次 ("last time") — while its mirror 下 marks "next" (下周, 下个月), a spatial up/down pair repurposed as Mandarin's default before/after marker for time.

examples.hanzi: 上周我感冒了,没有去上班。
examples.pinyin: Shàng zhōu wǒ gǎnmào le, méiyǒu qù shàngbān.
examples.english: I caught a cold last week and didn't go to work.

examples.hanzi: 你上周末在做什么?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shàng zhōumò zài zuò shénme?
examples.english: What did you do last weekend?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.

example.hanzi: 你为何不来？
example.pinyin: Nǐ wèi hé bù lái?
example.english: Why aren't you coming?
example.fact: 何 is the literary question word, which appears in modern Chinese only in set words: 如何 (how), 为何 (why), 任何 (any), 何必 (why bother), 何时 (when). In speech 什么 replaces it.

examples.hanzi: 你何时回来？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ héshí huílái?
examples.english: When will you be back?

examples.hanzi: 这里有何不可？
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu hé bùkě?
examples.english: What's wrong with that?

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).

example.hanzi: 手机没电了。
example.pinyin: Shǒujī méi diàn le.
example.english: The phone has run out of battery.
example.fact: 电 originally meant lightning, and it became the root of nearly every modern technology word: 电话, 电脑, 电视, 电影, 电梯. 没电 means out of battery or power.

examples.hanzi: 我家停电了，什么都做不了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā tíngdiàn le, shénme dōu zuò bu liǎo.
examples.english: The power is out at my home, so I can't do anything.

examples.hanzi: 这台电脑的电池只能用两个小时。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo de diànchí zhǐ néng yòng liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: This computer's battery lasts only two hours.

components.note: 司 (sī) is a sound clue for 词 cí and 饲 sì; as a word it means to manage, as in 公司 company.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 出租车司机很热情地跟我聊天。
example.pinyin: Chūzūchē sījī hěn rèqíng de gēn wǒ liáotiān.
example.english: The taxi driver chatted with me warmly.
example.fact: 司 alone is a very old word meaning "to take charge of, to manage" (as in 司令, "commander"), so 司机 literally means "the one in charge of the machine" — a fitting compositional image once cars, trains, and other engines started being called 机.

examples.hanzi: 司机把我们送到了酒店门口。
examples.pinyin: Sījī bǎ wǒmen sòng dào le jiǔdiàn ménkǒu.
examples.english: The driver took us to the hotel's front door.

examples.hanzi: 我叔叔是一名公交车司机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shūshu shì yì míng gōngjiāochē sījī.
examples.english: My uncle is a bus driver.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions done by hand, as in 找 look for, 拿 take, 抓 grab; 搜 is to search by hand.
叟 (sǒu) — same sound family — 搜 is sōu; 叟 also sounds out 艘 sōu.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.

example.hanzi: 警察搜查了整栋大楼。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá sōuchá le zhěng dòng dàlóu.
example.english: The police searched the entire building.
example.fact: 搜查 carries a formal, official register — used for police or authorities conducting a thorough, sanctioned search, often requiring a warrant (搜查令) — while the everyday, neutral verb 找 is simply "to look for" something you've misplaced.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在搜查他的房间。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài sōuchá tā de fángjiān.
examples.english: The police are searching his room.

examples.hanzi: 机场的工作人员搜查了每一个箱子。
examples.pinyin: Jīchǎng de gōngzuò rényuán sōuchá le měi yí ge xiāngzi.
examples.english: The airport staff searched every suitcase.

components.note: 生 (birth) — traditional 產 was 生 (birth) topped by 彦 for sound; the idea is giving birth, so bringing forth, as in 生产 and 产生.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这个决定可能会产生严重的后果。
example.pinyin: Zhège juédìng kěnéng huì chǎnshēng yánzhòng de hòuguǒ.
example.english: This decision could give rise to serious consequences.
example.fact: 产生 fuses "to produce" (产) with "to be born, to grow" (生) into a verb reserved for abstract outcomes — feelings, effects, problems — while 生产, the same two characters in reverse order, names the concrete industrial sense "to manufacture," a tidy example of character order alone splitting a pair into two different words.

examples.hanzi: 太多的糖会产生健康问题。
examples.pinyin: Tài duō de táng huì chǎnshēng jiànkāng wèntí.
examples.english: Too much sugar can cause health problems.

examples.hanzi: 他对这门课产生了兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè mén kè chǎnshēng le xìngqù.
examples.english: He developed an interest in this course.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这本书有一千页。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yǒu yì qiān yè.
example.english: This book has a thousand pages.
example.fact: Chinese counts in 万 (ten thousands), so 千 is always one level below that: 一万 = ten 千. 千万 means "ten million" as a number and "by all means" in warnings, as in 千万别忘了 (don't forget!).

examples.hanzi: 他一个月赚几千块钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí gè yuè zhuàn jǐqiān kuài qián.
examples.english: He earns several thousand yuan a month.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校有两千多个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu liǎng qiān duō gè xuésheng.
examples.english: Our school has more than two thousand students.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 巾 is a cloth radical, as in 帽 hat, 带 belt; 布 is cloth, and by extension to spread or announce, as in 宣布.

example.hanzi: 她用布做了一个包。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng bù zuò le yí ge bāo.
example.english: She made a bag out of cloth.
example.fact: 布 originally meant plain cloth (of cotton or hemp), in contrast to fancy silk, and later extended to spreading or announcing: 发布 (to release), 公布 (to publish), 布置 (to arrange).

examples.hanzi: 这块布很软，摸起来很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài bù hěn ruǎn, mō qǐlái hěn shūfu.
examples.english: This cloth is soft and feels nice to touch.

examples.hanzi: 公司明天会公布结果。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī míngtiān huì gōngbù jiéguǒ.
examples.english: The company will announce the results tomorrow.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.

example.hanzi: 我们生活在一个信息爆炸的时代。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen shēnghuó zài yí gè xìnxī bàozhà de shídài.
example.english: We live in an era of information explosion.
example.fact: 代 alone already means "a generation" (一代, "one generation") or "to take the place of" (代替) — 时代 extends that generational sense onto a whole historical span, so a 时代 is literally the length of time one "generation" or "era" occupies.

examples.hanzi: 手机改变了我们这个时代。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī gǎibiàn le wǒmen zhège shídài.
examples.english: Mobile phones have changed our era.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷常说他那个时代很苦。
examples.pinyin: Yéye cháng shuō tā nà ge shídài hěn kǔ.
examples.english: Grandpa often says that his time was hard.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
角 (horn) — 角 as in 解 untie: 触 first meant to butt with horns, then to touch.
虫 (chóng) — not a reliable sound clue — 触 is chù; the traditional 觸 had 蜀 (shǔ) giving the sound, and 虫 is its remnant.

example.hanzi: 医生提醒我们尽量少接触病人。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng wǒmen jǐnliàng shǎo jiēchù bìngrén.
example.english: The doctor reminded us to have as little contact with the patient as possible.
example.fact: 触 by itself already means "to touch, to bump into" — its component 角 (horn) reflects an original image of an animal butting with its horns — so 接触 layers 接 ("to receive, to connect") on top to generalize that physical contact into today's broader sense of being "in touch with" people, ideas, or information.

examples.hanzi: 他在工作中经常接触新朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngzuò zhōng jīngcháng jiēchù xīn péngyou.
examples.english: He often meets new people at work.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子不要接触火。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi bú yào jiēchù huǒ.
examples.english: Small children should not touch fire.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 一辆卡车堵住了整条路。
example.pinyin: Yí liàng kǎchē dǔzhù le zhěng tiáo lù.
example.english: A truck blocked the entire road.
example.fact: 卡 in 卡车 is widely believed to be a phonetic loan from English "car" — borrowed purely for its sound (kǎ) rather than any native meaning ("to jam, to block," as in 卡住) — joining other early 20th-century sound-based loanwords like 卡片 ("card") and 巴士 (bāshì, "bus").

examples.hanzi: 卡车司机在路边休息了一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Kǎchē sījī zài lùbiān xiūxi le yíhuìr.
examples.english: The truck driver rested for a while by the road.

examples.hanzi: 这辆卡车运来了很多水果。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng kǎchē yùn lái le hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: This truck brought in lots of fruit.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抢 is grabbing with the hands; also in 打, 拿, 抓.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 抢 is qiǎng; 仓 also sounds out 枪 qiāng and 创 chuàng.
力 (strength) — 力 means strength, here force — 劫 is to seize by force; compare 办, 动, 努.
去 (qù) — the sound has drifted — 劫 is jié, so 去 is only a rough clue.

example.hanzi: 那家银行昨晚被抢劫了。
example.pinyin: Nà jiā yínháng zuówǎn bèi qiǎngjié le.
example.english: That bank was robbed last night.
example.fact: Both halves of 抢劫 independently mean "to seize by force" — 抢 ("to grab, to snatch") and 劫 ("to plunder," as in 打劫, "to hold up, to rob") — stacking two near-synonymous verbs of violent taking into one word, the same reinforcing pattern seen in words like 喜欢 ("to like," from 喜 + 欢).

examples.hanzi: 有人在街上抢劫了一位老人。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén zài jiē shang qiǎngjié le yí wèi lǎorén.
examples.english: Someone robbed an old man on the street.

examples.hanzi: 这起抢劫案发生在昨天晚上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ qiǎngjié àn fāshēng zài zuótiān wǎnshang.
examples.english: This robbery took place last night.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 石 as in 破 break, 砖 brick: hard things colliding — 碰 is to bump into.
並 (bìng) — loose hint — 碰 is pèng; 並 (bìng) also sounds out 拼 pīn and 屏 píng.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 我在超市碰到了我的老同学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài chāoshì pèngdào le wǒ de lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: I ran into my old classmate at the supermarket.
example.fact: 碰到 leans toward an unplanned, chance encounter — bumping into a person or a problem by accident — while its near-synonym 遇到 stays neutral about whether the meeting was expected, and 见到 usually implies a planned visit; the core verb 碰 literally means "to bump, to collide," so a faint sense of accidental impact lingers in the word.

examples.hanzi: 今天早上我在路上碰到了老师。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang wǒ zài lù shang pèngdào le lǎoshī.
examples.english: This morning I ran into my teacher on the road.

examples.hanzi: 你没有碰到什么麻烦吧?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ méiyǒu pèngdào shénme máfan ba?
examples.english: You haven't run into any trouble, have you?

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.
父 (father) — a hand holding a stone axe, an image of the household head who works and rules.

example.hanzi: 他每个星期天都去教堂见神父。
example.pinyin: Tā měi gè xīngqītiān dōu qù jiàotáng jiàn shénfu.
example.english: He goes to church to see the priest every Sunday.
example.fact: 神父 likely began as a loan-translation of the Catholic title "Father" introduced by European missionaries — 神 ("god, divine") plus 父 ("father") mirrors the address term almost word for word — distinct from 牧师, the separate word reserved for a Protestant pastor.

examples.hanzi: 神父在教堂里为大家祈祷。
examples.pinyin: Shénfu zài jiàotáng lǐ wèi dàjiā qídǎo.
examples.english: The priest prayed for everyone in the church.

examples.hanzi: 神父,您能听我说几句话吗?
examples.pinyin: Shénfu, nín néng tīng wǒ shuō jǐ jù huà ma?
examples.english: Father, could you listen to what I have to say?

components.note: 见 (see) — 见 as in 现, 观, 觉; 规 first meant a compass, the drawing tool that sets the standard — hence rules, as in 规矩 compass and square.
夫 (fū) — loose sound hint — 规 is guī.
矢 (arrow) — 矩 is a carpenter's square; 矢 here hints at straight measuring — together with 规 compass: 规矩, rules.
巨 (jù) — near sound — 矩 is jǔ; 巨 also sounds out 距 jù and 拒 jù.

example.hanzi: 在这个家里,吃饭前洗手是规矩。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège jiā lǐ, chīfàn qián xǐshǒu shì guīju.
example.english: In this house, washing your hands before eating is the rule.
example.fact: 规矩 literally names two carpenter's tools — 规 the compass for drawing circles, 矩 the square for drawing right angles — the same pair found in the Mencius line 不以规矩,不能成方圆 ("without compass and square, one cannot form circles and squares"), the likely classical source of 规矩's modern sense "rule, standard."

examples.hanzi: 这里有这里的规矩,你要遵守。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu zhèlǐ de guīju, nǐ yào zūnshǒu.
examples.english: This place has its own rules, and you must follow them.

examples.hanzi: 他是个守规矩的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge shǒu guīju de háizi.
examples.english: He is a well-behaved child.

components.note: 之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 在众多申请者之中,只有三个人被选中。
example.pinyin: Zài zhòngduō shēnqǐngzhě zhīzhōng, zhǐyǒu sān gè rén bèi xuǎnzhòng.
example.english: Among all the applicants, only three people were selected.
example.fact: 之 is a fossil of Classical Chinese still alive today as a formal linking particle — functioning much like 的 does in everyday speech — so 之中 ("...'s midst") reads as the literary-register counterpart to the plainer, more colloquial 里面 or 当中.

examples.hanzi: 他生活在爱之中,所以很快乐。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēnghuó zài ài zhī zhōng, suǒyǐ hěn kuàilè.
examples.english: He lives surrounded by love, so he is very happy.

examples.hanzi: 人们在困难之中更需要朋友。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen zài kùnnan zhī zhōng gèng xūyào péngyou.
examples.english: People need friends even more in difficult times.

components.note: 火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 我们坐火车去北京。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò huǒchē qù Běijīng.
example.english: We're taking the train to Beijing.
example.fact: 火车 literally means "fire cart" — a name fixed in place by the earliest fire-driven steam locomotives, long before diesel and electric trains made the "fire" part literally inaccurate — the same naming logic behind 火柴 ("matches," literally "fire sticks").

examples.hanzi: 火车几点到北京?
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē jǐ diǎn dào Běijīng?
examples.english: What time does the train get to Beijing?

examples.hanzi: 我们得快点,火车马上就要开了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děi kuài diǎn, huǒchē mǎshàng jiù yào kāi le.
examples.english: We have to hurry, the train is about to leave.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.hanzi: 说实话,我不太喜欢这个计划。
example.pinyin: Shuōshíhuà, wǒ bú tài xǐhuan zhège jìhuà.
example.english: To be honest, I don't really like this plan.
example.fact: 说实话 almost always opens a sentence as a stand-alone discourse marker — much like English "honestly" or "to be frank" — signaling that a possibly blunt or unwelcome opinion is coming next, rather than literally commanding someone to "speak the truth."

examples.hanzi: 说实话,这道菜有点儿咸。
examples.pinyin: Shuō shíhuà, zhè dào cài yǒudiǎnr xián.
examples.english: To be honest, this dish is a bit salty.

examples.hanzi: 你能对我说实话吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng duì wǒ shuō shíhuà ma?
examples.english: Can you tell me the truth?

components.note: 十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".

example.hanzi: 你在看什么？
example.pinyin: Nǐ zài kàn shénme?
example.english: What are you looking at?
example.fact: In everyday speech 什 appears almost only inside 什么 (what). The word 什么 can be indefinite too: 有什么问题吗 (are there any problems?). 为什么 is "why". 什 as a number word (shí) is rare and old.

examples.hanzi: 你们在聊什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen zài liáo shénme?
examples.english: What are you chatting about?

examples.hanzi: 他为什么没来？
examples.pinyin: Tā wèishénme méi lái?
examples.english: Why didn't he come?

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 逃 is to run away.
兆 (zhào) — loose hint — 逃 is táo; 兆 also sounds out 桃 táo (same sound) and 跳 tiào.
足 (foot) — 足 (⻊ on the left) is the foot radical, as in 跳 jump, 路 road, 踢 kick; 跑 is to run.
包 (bāo) — near sound — 跑 is pǎo; 包 also sounds out 抱 bào, 饱 bǎo and 泡 pào.

example.hanzi: 那只猫看到狗就赶紧逃跑了。
example.pinyin: Nà zhī māo kàndào gǒu jiù gǎnjǐn táopǎo le.
example.english: The cat ran away as soon as it saw the dog.
example.fact: 逃跑 combines two verbs of escape that emphasize different things — 逃 ("to flee, to evade," as in 逃避, "to avoid") stresses getting away from danger, while 跑 ("to run") stresses the physical act of running — so the compound reads almost like "to flee by running," reinforcing both the motive and the method.

examples.hanzi: 小偷看到警察就逃跑了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu kàndào jǐngchá jiù táopǎo le.
examples.english: The thief ran away as soon as he saw the police.

examples.hanzi: 你逃跑也没有用,我们会找到你的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ táopǎo yě méiyǒu yòng, wǒmen huì zhǎodào nǐ de.
examples.english: It's no use running away, we will find you.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — marks grain and food, as in 粉, 粮, 饭; 糖 is sugar, once made from grain.
唐 (táng) gives the sound exactly: 糖 táng, also in 塘 táng.

example.hanzi: 她不吃太多糖。
example.pinyin: Tā bù chī tài duō táng.
example.english: She doesn't eat too much sugar.
example.fact: 糖 means both sugar and candy: 白糖 (white sugar), 糖果 (sweets), 棉花糖 (candy floss). Diabetes is 糖尿病, literally "sugar urine disease", and 糖葫芦 is the candied hawthorn skewer.

examples.hanzi: 咖啡里请放一点糖。
examples.pinyin: Kāfēi lǐ qǐng fàng yìdiǎn táng.
examples.english: Please put a little sugar in the coffee.

examples.hanzi: 小孩子都喜欢吃糖。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi dōu xǐhuan chī táng.
examples.english: Kids all like eating candy.

components.note: 旧 (simplified 舊) — old; the old sound part 臼 (jiù) also gives 舅 jiù (uncle).

example.hanzi: 这件衣服太旧了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài jiù le.
example.english: This garment is too old.
example.fact: 旧 is the opposite of 新 and refers to things worn with age (旧书, 旧衣服). 老 is for living beings or long-standing things. 念旧 means sentimental about the past and 怀旧 means nostalgic.

examples.hanzi: 我穿旧鞋去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chuān jiù xié qù páshān.
examples.english: I wear old shoes to go hiking.

examples.hanzi: 他还住在旧房子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā hái zhù zài jiù fángzi lǐ.
examples.english: He still lives in the old house.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 这个问题不属于我们部门负责。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí bù shǔyú wǒmen bùmén fùzé.
example.english: This issue isn't our department's responsibility.
example.fact: 门 broadened from its literal sense "door, gate" into a common suffix marking a category or field (部门 "department", 专门 "specialized", 门类 "category") — the underlying image treats each division of an organization as its own separate "doorway" into it.

examples.hanzi: 我在销售部门工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài xiāoshòu bùmén gōngzuò.
examples.english: I work in the sales department.

examples.hanzi: 请你联系一下相关部门。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ liánxì yíxià xiāngguān bùmén.
examples.english: Please contact the relevant department.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the bottom part, as in 灯 lamp and 炎 flame. The dictionary lists fire as the hint: a spirit like a flickering flame, as in 灵魂.
彐 (snout) — the top part, a stroke group as in 当 and 归. 灵 simplifies 靈, so this shape is not a sound clue. Memory aid: a hand over a flame, feeling a spirit.

example.hanzi: 这个方法很灵。
example.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn líng.
example.english: This method works really well.
example.fact: 灵 as a spoken adjective means effective, said of remedies or tricks: 很灵. It forms 灵活 (flexible), 灵感 (inspiration), 心灵 (mind, spirit) and 灵魂 (soul).

examples.hanzi: 他的脑子很灵。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nǎozi hěn líng.
examples.english: He is very quick-witted.

examples.hanzi: 这个药很灵，我吃了就好了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yào hěn líng, wǒ chī le jiù hǎo le.
examples.english: This medicine is effective; I got better after taking it.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — the left part and radical, as in 船 ship. Meaning hint: boats, a tray.
殳 (weapon/tool in hand) — the right part, also in 段 and 投 (throw). Story: handling a tool on a tray to sort things into kinds, hence 'sort, kind'; memory aid only.

example.hanzi: 他像孩子一般高兴。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng háizi yìbān gāoxìng.
example.english: He is happy like a child.
example.fact: 般 is nearly always inside 一般 (ordinary, usually). It also marks similes with 如 / 像 ... 般, as in 雪一般白 (white as snow) and 如梦般 (dreamlike).

examples.hanzi: 他们兄弟俩长得一般高。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen xiōngdì liǎ zhǎng de yìbān gāo.
examples.english: The two brothers are about the same height.

examples.hanzi: 今天的天气一般，不冷也不热。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì yìbān, bù lěng yě bú rè.
examples.english: The weather today is so-so, neither cold nor hot.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth radical — a base is something solid on the ground, as in 地, 城, 块.
其 (qí) — loose hint — 基 is jī; 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 旗 qí.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 这是每个员工都应该知道的基本规则。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì měi gè yuángōng dōu yīnggāi zhīdào de jīběn guīzé.
example.english: These are basic rules every employee should know.
example.fact: 基本 stacks two near-synonymous "foundation" images — 基 (a base one builds on, as in 基础) and 本 (a tree's root, as in 根本) — into one word, and it does double duty as both an adjective ("basic") and an adverb meaning "basically" (基本上 makes this adverbial sense explicit).

examples.hanzi: 我只会说几句基本的中文。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ huì shuō jǐ jù jīběn de Zhōngwén.
examples.english: I can only say a few basic phrases in Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 这两种方法基本一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng zhǒng fāngfǎ jīběn yíyàng.
examples.english: These two methods are basically the same.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain — rent was originally paid in grain, as in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
且 (qiě) — loose hint — 租 is zū; 且 also sounds out 组 zǔ and 祖 zǔ.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 我们打了一辆出租车去机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎ le yí liàng chūzūchē qù jīchǎng.
example.english: We took a taxi to the airport.
example.fact: 出租车 literally means "a vehicle rented out" (出租, "to rent out" + 车, "vehicle"), but the far more common way to talk about actually catching one in casual Mainland speech is the verb 打车 ("to hail a taxi," literally "to hit a car"); 的士, a phonetic loan from English "taxi", is the everyday term instead in Cantonese-speaking regions like Guangzhou and Hong Kong.

examples.hanzi: 这里很难打到出租车。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ hěn nán dǎdào chūzūchē.
examples.english: It's hard to catch a taxi here.

examples.hanzi: 出租车比公共汽车贵一些。
examples.pinyin: Chūzūchē bǐ gōnggòng qìchē guì yìxiē.
examples.english: A taxi is a bit more expensive than a bus.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding the reins.
空 (kōng) is a close sound clue for kòng; 空 also in 腔 qiāng and 孔 kǒng.

example.hanzi: 他控制不了自己的脾气。
example.pinyin: Tā kòngzhì bu liǎo zìjǐ de píqi.
example.english: He can't control his temper.
example.fact: 控 appears in 控制 (control), 遥控 (remote control) and 控告 (to accuse). In recent slang it is a suffix for "fan of": 颜控 is someone obsessed with good looks, borrowed from the Japanese コン.

examples.hanzi: 你要控制好自己的情绪。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào kòngzhì hǎo zìjǐ de qíngxù.
examples.english: You need to keep your emotions under control.

examples.hanzi: 警察控告他偷了东西。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá kònggào tā tōu le dōngxi.
examples.english: The police accused him of stealing.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood — 析 is to split wood with an axe 斤, then to analyse by breaking things apart, as in 分析.
斤 (jīn) — 斤 is an axe and a weak sound hint — 析 is xī.

example.hanzi: 请分析一下这个问题的原因。
example.pinyin: Qǐng fēnxī yíxià zhège wèntí de yuányīn.
example.english: Please analyze the reasons behind this problem.
example.fact: 析 alone already means "to split apart" — its component 斤 pictures an axe splitting the wood 木 beside it — so 分析 ("to divide" + "to split") builds the abstract idea of "analysis" out of two very concrete images of physically breaking something into pieces.

examples.hanzi: 经理让我们分析一下这个月的数据。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ ràng wǒmen fēnxī yíxià zhège yuè de shùjù.
examples.english: The manager asked us to analyze this month's data.

examples.hanzi: 他的分析很有道理。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fēnxī hěn yǒu dàolǐ.
examples.english: His analysis makes a lot of sense.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.

example.hanzi: 他为这次成功付出了很大的代价。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè cì chénggōng fùchū le hěn dà de dàijià.
example.english: He paid a great price for this success.
example.fact: 代价 almost always names a figurative cost — sacrifice, consequence, effort — rather than a literal shop price, which is why it pairs naturally with 付出 (also in this batch) in the fixed phrase 付出代价 ("to pay a price"); for an actual price tag, Chinese uses 价格 instead.

examples.hanzi: 这次旅行的代价比我想的要高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng de dàijià bǐ wǒ xiǎng de yào gāo.
examples.english: The cost of this trip was higher than I expected.

examples.hanzi: 他不惜任何代价也要救她。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xī rènhé dàijià yě yào jiù tā.
examples.english: He would save her at any cost.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.

example.hanzi: 这个地区经常下雪。
example.pinyin: Zhège dìqū jīngcháng xià xuě.
example.english: This region often gets snow.
example.fact: 区 is also a standard tier of Chinese urban administration — in a city like Beijing or Shanghai, a 区 ("district") sits directly below the municipal 市 — so 地区, literally "earth" plus "district," can mean either a loose geographic area or, more formally, a specific administrative unit.

examples.hanzi: 这个地区的夏天特别热。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de xiàtiān tèbié rè.
examples.english: Summers in this region are especially hot.

examples.hanzi: 我们公司在很多地区都有分店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài hěn duō dìqū dōu yǒu fēndiàn.
examples.english: Our company has branches in many regions.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the flesh/body radical (月 in 脸, 脚, 肚); 背 is the back of the body.
北 (běi) — near sound — 背 is bèi; 北 originally pictured two people back to back, which is the sense of 背.
反 (opposite) — 反 means opposite or against — 叛 is going against, rebelling.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 叛 is pàn; 半 also sounds out 伴 bàn and 拌 bàn.

example.hanzi: 他背叛了自己最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā bèipàn le zìjǐ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: He betrayed his own best friend.
example.fact: 叛 alone already means "to rebel, to revolt" (as in 叛乱, "rebellion"), built from 反 ("opposite, contrary") plus a phonetic element — 背叛 adds 背 ("the back," extended to "to turn one's back on") to sharpen that rebellion into the specific, personal sense of betraying someone who trusted you.

examples.hanzi: 我不会背叛信任我的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú huì bèipàn xìnrèn wǒ de rén.
examples.english: I will never betray those who trust me.

examples.hanzi: 她觉得男朋友背叛了她。
examples.pinyin: Tā juéde nán péngyou bèipàn le tā.
examples.english: She feels her boyfriend betrayed her.

components.note: 走 (walk) — marks walking and going, as in 起 rise, 赶 hurry; 趟 is a trip, as in 去一趟.
尚 (shàng) — loose sound hint (tàng vs shàng); 尚 also sounds out 躺 tǎng and 堂 táng.

example.hanzi: 我去了一趟北京。
example.pinyin: Wǒ qù le yí tàng Běijīng.
example.english: I made a trip to Beijing.
example.fact: 趟 counts a trip there and back: 去一趟, 跑一趟. It also counts scheduled runs of trains or buses: 这趟火车 (this train service). It differs from 次, which counts any occasion.

examples.hanzi: 我去过两趟上海。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù guo liǎng tàng Shànghǎi.
examples.english: I have been to Shanghai twice.

examples.hanzi: 下一趟火车几点开？
examples.pinyin: Xià yí tàng huǒchē jǐ diǎn kāi?
examples.english: What time does the next train leave?

components.note: 大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.
土 (earth) — ground and building sites: 地, 场, 块; 堂 is a raised hall.
尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; same part in 常 cháng, 掌 zhǎng, 堂 táng.

example.hanzi: 她说这个海边小镇就像天堂一样。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō zhège hǎibiān xiǎozhèn jiù xiàng tiāntáng yíyàng.
example.english: She said this seaside town is just like paradise.
example.fact: 天堂 (literally "sky hall") entered Chinese through Buddhist and later Christian loan-translation for the idea of a heavenly afterlife, and it's paired in everyday speech with its opposite 地狱 ("hell," literally "earth prison") — a sky-versus-earth contrast that echoes the up/down cosmology found across many world religions.

examples.hanzi: 对孩子们来说,游乐园就是天堂。
examples.pinyin: Duì háizimen lái shuō, yóulèyuán jiù shì tiāntáng.
examples.english: To kids, an amusement park is heaven.

examples.hanzi: 这里的风景美得像天堂。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng měi de xiàng tiāntáng.
examples.english: The scenery here is as beautiful as paradise.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 拍 is clapping or patting with the hand, also used for filming and taking photos.
白 (bái) — loose hint — 拍 is pāi; 白 also sounds out 伯 bó and 怕 pà.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摄 is taking hold, then capturing on camera, as in 拍摄.

example.hanzi: 这部电影是在云南拍摄的。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shì zài Yúnnán pāishè de.
example.english: This movie was filmed in Yunnan.
example.fact: 拍摄 is the formal, professional register for filming or photography — used for movies, documentaries, or news coverage — while 拍 alone is the everyday, casual verb (拍照片, "to take a photo") that any tourist with a phone would use for a quick snapshot.

examples.hanzi: 我们正在拍摄一部短片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài pāishè yí bù duǎnpiàn.
examples.english: We are shooting a short film.

examples.hanzi: 这张照片是在雪山上拍摄的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn shì zài xuěshān shang pāishè de.
examples.english: This photo was taken on a snowy mountain.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
车 (cart, simplified 車) — vehicles and transport: 转 turn, 输 transport, 较 compare; 轻 was a light cart.
The right half is a short form of 巠 (jīng), the sound part in 经 jīng, 径 jìng and 茎 jīng — a loose clue for qīng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 现在很多年轻人喜欢在网上购物。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō niánqīngrén xǐhuan zài wǎngshàng gòuwù.
example.english: Nowadays many young people like shopping online.
example.fact: 轻 in 年轻 literally means "light (in weight)" — its component 车 preserves an old image of a light, nimble cart — so "young" in Mandarin is built on a metaphor of youth as an unburdened, light stage of life, set against its opposite 年老 ("old," carrying a sense of being weathered and worn).

examples.hanzi: 年轻人应该多读书,多旅行。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīngrén yīnggāi duō dúshū, duō lǚxíng.
examples.english: Young people should read more and travel more.

examples.hanzi: 这家咖啡店里全是年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēidiàn lǐ quán shì niánqīngrén.
examples.english: This café is full of young people.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.
至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.

example.hanzi: 长期缺乏运动可能导致健康问题。
example.pinyin: Chángqī quēfá yùndòng kěnéng dǎozhì jiànkāng wèntí.
example.english: A long-term lack of exercise can lead to health problems.
example.fact: 导致 leans heavily toward negative or undesirable outcomes — illness, accidents, failure — while a neutral or positive causal chain more naturally takes 使 or 让 instead, which is why native speakers notice something slightly off in a sentence like 努力导致成功 ("hard work led to success") even though it's grammatically fine.

examples.hanzi: 大雨导致了很多航班取消。
examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ dǎozhì le hěn duō hángbān qǔxiāo.
examples.english: The heavy rain caused many flights to be canceled.

examples.hanzi: 睡得太少会导致头疼。
examples.pinyin: Shuì de tài shǎo huì dǎozhì tóuténg.
examples.english: Sleeping too little can lead to headaches.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脑 brain, 脚 foot); 脸 is a body part, the face.
佥 (qiān) — loose hint — 脸 is liǎn; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn, 险 xiǎn and 验 yàn, all ending in -ǎn.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 听到这个好消息,他脸上露出了笑容。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, tā liǎnshàng lùchū le xiàoróng.
example.english: Hearing the good news, a smile appeared on his face.
example.fact: 脸上 attaches the location suffix 上 ("on top of") to 脸 ("face") to name not the face itself but whatever appears on its surface — an expression, a smile, a blush — which is why Chinese almost always says a smile "appeared 脸上" rather than describing the face directly, treating expressions as things that surface on it.

examples.hanzi: 她脸上带着一点儿不好意思。
examples.pinyin: Tā liǎn shang dài zhe yìdiǎnr bù hǎoyìsi.
examples.english: She had a slightly embarrassed look on her face.

examples.hanzi: 你脸上有一点儿奶油。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ liǎn shang yǒu yìdiǎnr nǎiyóu.
examples.english: You have a bit of cream on your face.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 老师应该平等地对待每一个学生。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yīnggāi píngděng de duìdài měi yí gè xuésheng.
example.english: Teachers should treat every student equally.
example.fact: 对待 always takes a person, or something personified, as its object — how you treat a person, an issue, or an animal — and can't be used the way English "treat" sometimes is for medical care; for that sense Chinese switches entirely to 治疗.

examples.hanzi: 你应该好好对待你的家人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi hǎohāo duìdài nǐ de jiārén.
examples.english: You should treat your family well.

examples.hanzi: 我们要认真对待这次考试。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào rènzhēn duìdài zhè cì kǎoshì.
examples.english: We should take this exam seriously.
